target: 5-file reproducer at 7c0bba2, host tree in the bisect worktree, --no-flash for every measurement

ruled_out.firmware: 578ad8b and 2b60129 have identical layout a689f7f2a69889a4 - the same generated code by today's #5 result
ruled_out.board_uptime: 90 min then, 40 min now, and 0/10 right after a flash
ruled_out.host_tree: the worktree sat at 7c0bba2 throughout, verified clean

not_separated: thermal state - the board ran three full suites and many reflashes this afternoon
something cumulative in the host that a reboot would clear and a reflash does not

void_experiment.what: promotion of the daemon's _read_loop, which rt.promote() supports on this bench (class=0x80, thread=time-critical, timer=1ms) and host/daemon/ never calls
void_experiment.verdict: VOID. Both arms null because the lever was not firing. Pre-registered as '0-1/10 is a drop', so the promoted arm alone would have been published as promotion closing the context lever - on an experiment whose control shows there was no lever to close. It survived only because a fresh baseline had been promised for an unrelated reason (firmware had moved).

what_it_costs.bisect: stands. Its four arms were minutes apart inside one window and separated cleanly; whatever the third variable is, it did not change inside that half hour.
what_it_costs.fix_validation: the 0/20 and clean suite were in the same window as the 6/10, so that contrast is real - but any LATER null at the fix is worth less than stated.
what_it_costs.contention_4x: taken after 17:00, outside the window. Should be read as UNMEASURED rather than as a null, which weakens the 'Windows is the odd host' row this bench contributed.

means: This bench had a reproducer for about half an hour and cannot currently re-arm it. linux-x1's and mac-bench's levers both have positive controls that fire on demand; this one does not, and did not when it was used.

warm_bench_after_full_suite.note: the suite itself was green - 583 passed, including test_a_client_that_stops_reading, which failed 2 of 2 full suites this afternoon

eliminated: board uptime (90 min firing, 40 min not)
a warm bench / heavy prior activity
remaining: host state a reboot would clear - the only untested candidate, and one that needs an action bigger than an experiment
cross_bench_fade: WITHDRAWN. mac-bench found their fade series confounded by their own fix landing at 16:36 mid-series, so every later number is a post-fix number; their concurrent pair is 3/8 against 1/8, p = 0.57, which separates neither hypothesis. And linux-x1 checked: their contention lever has NOT faded - 25 of 44 at 2x across five arms this evening, 57%, still firing at 23:20. So the synchronisation argument had no second leg and no third.
what_survives: One bench faded, at one commit, unexplained. Every windows-desk arm was at 7c0bba2 with the host tree pinned in the worktree and verified clean, so this fade is not confounded the way mac-bench s was: 6/10 afternoon against 0/28 evening, p = 0.00035.
my_error: Pooled another bench arms without asking whether their commit had moved under them - the #44 pooling error, which I had corrected on that issue earlier the same day. Two benches reporting a lever gone within an hour is a striking coincidence, and I treated the coincidence as the finding rather than as the thing to check. The check was one question and I listed the repository moving as a candidate without asking it.
stopping_because: every further arm is a null from an instrument already established as unable to fire, which is what #58 exists to warn about. Continuing would generate numbers with the shape of evidence and none of the content.
first_thing_next_session: run the reproducer BEFORE anything else on a freshly booted host. If it fires, host state is the answer and this bench has a re-arm procedure. If not, the afternoon 6-of-10 needs an explanation none of the three benches currently has.
